title: QBR Actionable Telemetry Playbook for Model Updates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the telemetry signals, dashboards, pre-QBR validation checks, and an operational runbook for handling model updates that will be reviewed in Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering, and Platform/Observability engineering teams who coordinate on customer-impacting model changes.

Purpose:
- Ensure QBRs produce concrete, prioritized actions tied to measurable telemetry.
- Reduce time-to-action when model updates introduce quality regressions or cost regressions.
- Provide reproducible validation steps to inform customer communications and rollback decisions.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private tenants where model version changes are scheduled or detected in production.
- Covers telemetry ingestion, dashboarding, pre-QBR validation, QBR agenda items, and post-QBR action tracking.
- Does NOT replace live incident runbooks for Sev1 customer outages; escalate to incident channels if SLO breaches occur.

Definitions:
- Canary cohort: A small subset of traffic routed to the new model variant for early signals.
- Cost delta: Measured change in average token cost per 1k tokens across a tenant or cohort.
- Fidelity regression: Any statistically significant drop in model-quality signals (see telemetry).
- SLO impact window: 24h rolling window used for SLA/SLO reconciliation pre-QBR.

Owners & Contacts:
- Playbook owner: Aisha Patel (Customer Success)
- Observability contact: Marcus Li (Eng Platform)
- Model-onboarding contact: Sophie Romero (Applied ML)
- Escalation lead (on-call): see /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks for rotation

Primary telemetry signals (minimum set to collect for QBR):
1) Performance/Latency
- p50/p90/p95/99 request latency (ms) by model_version, region, deployment_type
- Tail token generation latency (per-token)
- Cold-start frequency (starts per hour)

2) Cost & Throughput
- Tokens generated per minute and tokens per request distribution
- Average cost per 1k tokens (pre- and post-update)
- GPU utilization and queued requests by serving-pool

3) Quality & Safety
- Eval pass rate on customer-defined evaluation prompts (pass/fail)
- Hallucination flag rate (automated detectors) and manual triage counts
- Rejection and toxicity rates (policy throttle events)
- Behavioral deltas: intent-preservation score, entity-extraction F1 (if available)

4) Customer Experience Signals
- Request success rate (2xx vs 4xx/5xx) and error breakdowns by model_version
- End-user feature-level metrics (e.g., conversion rate for generation-driven flow)
- Customer-reported quality tickets and time-to-first-response

5) Canary & Cohort Metrics
- Percentage of traffic served by canary, cohort-specific latency/cost/quality metrics
- Divergence score between baseline and canary across key signals

Minimum alert thresholds (tunable per-customer):
- Latency: p95 increased > 40% vs baseline for 30 minutes across a tenant -> paged alert
- Cost: cost per 1k tokens increased > 25% and absolute increase > $0.10 per 1k for 2 hours -> page CS/FinOps
- Quality: eval pass rate drop >= 5 percentage points with p < 0.01 over 24h -> page ML lead
- Error rate: success rate < 99% (tenant-level) sustained 15 minutes -> paged SRE

Pre-QBR validation checklist (2 weeks prior to QBR):
1) Telemetry completeness:
   - Confirm ingestion for all signals above for the last 30 days. Missing metrics must be flagged and owner assigned.
2) Baseline calculation:
   - Compute baseline baselines for latency/cost/quality over last 30 days and 7-day rolling windows.
3) Canary harvest:
   - Ensure at least one 1–2% canary window or synthetic traffic run produced data for the new model.
4) Customer impact sampling:
   - Select 3–5 representative customers (by usage and contract tier) and prepare a short summary of impact.
5) Analytics deck and artifacts:
   - Attach dashboards, SQL queries, and sample request/response pairs (pseudonymized).

QBR agenda (45–60 minutes slot recommended):
- 0–5m: Context and summary of planned model updates since last QBR (owner: Product/ML)
- 5–20m: Telemetry highlights and deltas (owner: Observability) — show cost/latency/quality comparisons and canary divergence score
- 20–30m: Customer impact snapshots and open support tickets (owner: Customer Success)
- 30–40m: Action items and triage decisions (rollout, mitigation, communication)
- 40–60m: Timeline and owners for remediation or further validation tests

During QBR: decision matrix for model update outcomes
- Decision factors: cost delta, fidelity regression magnitude, SLO breach probability, number of affected customers, contractual implications.
- Possible outcomes:
  - Proceed to full rollout: no significant deltas and positive or neutral signals.
  - Hold and extend canary: minor regressions or insufficient data.
  - Partial rollback (subset of tenants): regressions isolated to certain cohorts/regions.
  - Full rollback: large regression or SLA breach.

Post-QBR action tracking (owner assignments & SLAs):
- Low priority: create CS/Docs ticket to update client guidance (owner CS, SLA 30 days)
- Medium priority: engineering investigation and mitigation (owner Eng Platform/Runtime, SLA 7 days)
- High priority: Hotfix/rollback and customer comms (owner Eng SRE + CS, SLA 24–72 hours)

Operational runbook for an automated detection during QBR window:
1) Detection phase:
   - Alert fires into PagerDuty and creates a JIRA with template label "model-update-delta".
   - CS and ML leads are auto-notified via #cs-model-updates channel.
2) Triage phase (first 60 mins):
   - Verify metric drift using provided sample queries.
   - Pull 50 random request/response pairs (pseudonymized) for manual review.
   - If error or latency that impacts SLO: open incident and follow oncall runbook.
3) Remediation phase (1–24 hrs):
   - If regression isolated to canary: increase sampling to collect more data or rollback canary.
   - If regression global and high severity: trigger controlled rollback and notify customers.

Customer communication templates (short):
- When notifying about planned update: "We plan to upgrade model XYZ in region EU-W at 2026-03-15T22:00Z. We will run a canary at 2% traffic and monitor latency, cost, and quality metrics. Contact your CS rep if you have constraints."
- When notifying about detected regression: "We observed an increase in generation latency and a regression in quality signals after the recent model update. We are investigating and will provide a mitigation plan within 24 hours."

Dashboards and sample queries (appendix)
- PromQL (latency p95 by model):
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_ms_bucket{job="inference"}[5m])) by (le, model_version))
```

- SQL (example) — baseline vs new model cost per 1k tokens (Postgres)
```
SELECT model_version,
  avg(tokens) as avg_tokens,
  avg(cost_per_1k) as avg_cost_per_1k,
  count(*) as requests
FROM inference_request_metrics
WHERE tenant_id = '<<TENANT_ID>>' AND ts >= now() - interval '30 days'
GROUP BY model_version
ORDER BY avg_cost_per_1k desc;
```

- Sample telemetry JSON schema (ingest):
```
{
  "ts": "2026-02-01T18:23:03Z",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-123",
  "model_version": "redwood-1.2.3",
  "request_id": "req-abc",
  "tokens_in": 14,
  "tokens_out": 68,
  "latency_ms": 412,
  "cost": 0.00083,
  "eval_pass": true,
  "hallucination_flag": false
}
```

Acceptance criteria for QBR actions:
- Every high-priority action must have an owner and a due date within 72 hours.
- Medium actions must include a linked investigation ticket with expected completion within 7 days.
- All mitigations that affect customer SLAs must be recorded in the customer ticket and legal/finance notified if credits are likely.

Metrics to be archived with QBR:
- Baseline vs post-update p95 latency change percentage
- Delta in avg cost per 1k tokens and delta in tokens generated per request
- Eval pass rate change and hallucination rate change
- Number of customers affected and number of open tickets tied to the change

Appendix: quick reference checklist (one-pager for QBR slides)
- Telemetry: Complete for 30 days (Y/N)
- Canary data present (Y/N) — sample size >= 1k requests or 48h of 1–2% traffic
- Cost delta % (number) and absolute $/1k
- Quality delta (eval pass rate delta)
- Top 3 affected customers and summary
- Proposed next action and owner

Related documents & links:

- QBR Template and Operational Checklist: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/health-and-qbr/qbr-template-and-operational-checklist-2026

Notes & rationale:
- This playbook assumes instrumentation parity across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. If a private deployment cannot provide one of the telemetry signals, mark as an exception and capture compensating controls in the QBR artifacts.
- Thresholds are intentionally conservative; owners should calibrate to tenant-specific baselines before using for paging.
